The logarithms share the same base, so we can combine them using the quotient rule, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{log}⁡(x)-\operatorname{log}⁡(2) & =1 \\ \operatorname{log}⁡(\frac{x}{2}) & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we solve the equation for $x$ using the usual methods.

$$
\begin{aligned}{10}^{\operatorname{log}⁡(x/2)} & ={10}^{1} \\ \frac{x}{2} & =10 \\ x & =20\end{aligned}
$$
